articles.title: Home Assistant fixes delayed and repeated Apple Watch actions
articles.dek: Commands take priority over background updates, and a missing reply no longer automatically repeats an action.
body: An action started on Apple Watch could run on the paired iPhone about 50 seconds later, after the watch had already reported failure. Home Assistant gives user commands priority over sensor reports and watch-face updates, and removes a request from the waiting queue if it is cancelled or expires before sending.

If the iPhone receives an action but does not report back in time, the watch stops automatically repeating requests that might run the action twice. Instead, it asks the person to check whether the action ran before trying again.

Bruno Pantaleão Gonçalves corrects this behavior in the iPhone relay described in the September 23 edition. That earlier change restored connections inside some home networks; this one addresses unexpected delayed or duplicate actions.

articles.title: ESPHome matches infrared air-conditioner modes to the equipment
articles.dek: Makers can hide an unusable automatic mode or explicitly retain it on a cooling-only unit.
body: Makers configuring infrared air conditioners in ESPHome gain an explicit choice of whether to offer the combined heat-and-cool mode. The mode stops appearing by default when a configuration disables heating or cooling, avoiding a control that the equipment may not support.

Some cooling-only units do have an automatic mode, while some units that heat and cool do not. Leonardo Rivera adds supports_heat_cool across the shared infrared platform, including Gree and Mitsubishi, to handle those exceptions.

Automations or voice commands requesting a mode removed by the new default need attention. Setting supports_heat_cool: true retains it where the equipment supports it; false hides it even on a unit configured for both heating and cooling.

articles.title: Forecast.Solar’s library keeps production estimates on the right day
articles.dek: Forecast.Solar’s Python library groups estimates by the solar installation’s local date.
body: Forecast.Solar’s Python library corrects daily production estimates for installations outside UTC. It previously requested totals grouped by UTC date, which could move a local morning’s forecast into the preceding day and give misleading figures for today and tomorrow.

Dex changes the request to use the installation’s timezone. In a comparison against the live service for a Sydney installation, the September 20 estimate was 12,059 watt-hours when grouped locally, instead of 9,454 in the UTC group. This is Dex’s first contribution to the library, reviewed by Klaas Schoute.

articles.title: Home Assistant controls Hot Spring jets and heating modes
articles.dek: Compatible spas gain pump-speed choices and heater modes, including cooling when a CoolZone heat pump is present.
body: Hot Spring spa owners gain Home Assistant controls for each enabled jet pump and for supported heater modes. Dual-speed pumps offer off, low and high settings, while single-speed pumps offer off and high.
Christophe Gagnier adds the spa’s heat-saver, boosted-heat and automatic modes where the hardware supports them. A chill option appears only when a CoolZone heat pump is installed.

articles.title: ESPHome repairs LibreTiny builds in its Docker image
articles.dek: A conflicting library blocks some firmware builds that combine MQTT messaging with a Wi-Fi setup portal.
body: ESPHome’s standalone Docker image stops supplying a conflicting networking library that prevents some LibreTiny firmware from building. The reported combination uses MQTT messaging alongside the captive portal for Wi-Fi setup; a library intended for ESP32 devices was taking precedence over the correct one.

J. Nick Koston removes the unused global library installation from the Docker and development-container images. He verified that a BK72xx configuration which fails in the 2026.9.0 image builds with the correction. The Home Assistant add-on already uses a separate, empty global library folder.

articles.title: ESPHome tunes temperature-control behavior while a device runs
articles.dek: Makers gain controls for tuning a device’s response near its target temperature without stopping it.
body: Makers using ESPHome’s PID climate controller gain actions for changing its response close to the target temperature while the device runs. These configured actions adjust the near-target range, called the deadband, and how strongly the controller responds inside it.

New sensors report those settings so a configuration can expose the values being used. Contributor ngolf supplies the implementation and accompanying guide in their first contributions to the ESPHome code and documentation repositories, reviewed by J. Nick Koston.

articles.title: Music Assistant flags a broken ListenBrainz connection
articles.dek: A rejected token prompts attention instead of silently losing listening-history updates.
body: Music Assistant alerts ListenBrainz users when a reset or revoked token stops their listening history from reaching the service. The connection previously appeared healthy while every played track triggered another failed submission.
Marcel van der Veldt makes the plugin stop submitting listens and mark itself as needing attention, prompting the listener to update its configuration.

roadmapUpdates.title: A prototype explores “all except” automation targets
roadmapUpdates.summary: Contributor integratedautomations proposes an “Except” section for leaving devices, areas or labels out of an automation target. The community prototype explores gaps in Home Assistant’s target-exclusion design; the opportunity remains in Shaping, without a recorded project decision to adopt it.
